questions.title: Temperature self Fahrenheit
questions.description:
A `Temperature` class stores `@celsius` set in the constructor and defines a class method `self.to_fahrenheit(c)` that returns `(c * 9.0 / 5.0) + 32.0`. The instance method `in_fahrenheit` calls `self.class.to_fahrenheit(@celsius)`. Read a celsius float and print the fahrenheit value formatted to two decimals.

Input Format:
Line 1: float celsius.

Output Format:
`X.XX` fahrenheit value to two decimals.

Constraints:
-1000.0 <= c <= 1000.0.
questions.sourcecode:
class Temperature
  def initialize(celsius)
    @celsius = celsius
  end
  def self.to_fahrenheit(c)
    (c * 9.0 / 5.0) + 32.0
  end
  def in_fahrenheit
    self.class.to_fahrenheit(@celsius)
  end
end
c = gets.to_f

questions.title: Point Manhattan Distance
questions.description:
A `Point` class stores `@x`, `@y` set in the constructor with read methods `x` and `y`. The instance method `distance_to(other)` returns the Manhattan distance `|x1-x2| + |y1-y2|`. Read four integers x1 y1 x2 y2 and print the distance.

Input Format:
Line 1: four integers separated by spaces.

Output Format:
The integer Manhattan distance.

Constraints:
-1000 <= x, y <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
class Point
  def initialize(x, y)
    @x = x
    @y = y
  end
  def distance_to(other)
    (@x - other.x).abs + (@y - other.y).abs
  end
  def x; @x end
  def y; @y end
end

p1 = Point.new(x1, y1)
p2 = Point.new(x2, y2)
puts p1.distance_to(p2)

questions.title: Stack Push Pop Operations
questions.description:
Implement a `Stack` class backed by an instance variable array `@items` set in `initialize`. Provide instance methods `push(x)`, `pop`, `peek`, `size`, and `empty?`. Read n then n commands (`push X`, `pop`, `peek`, `size`, or `empty`). For each command print the corresponding result line.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: a command (and integer arg for push).

Output Format:
One output line per command.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; -1000 <= X <= 1000.
questions.input2:
6
push 1
push 2
push 3
pop
pop
size
questions.whitelist: def push, def pop, def initialize
questions.sourcecode:
class Stack
  def initialize
    @items = []
  end
  def push(x)
    @items.push(x)
  end
  def pop
    @items.pop
  end
  def peek
    @items.last
  end
  def size
    @items.length
  end
  def empty?
    @items.empty?
  end
end
n = gets.to_i
stack = Stack.new
n.times do
  cmd = gets.split
  case cmd[0]
  when "push"
    stack.push(cmd[1].to_i)
    puts "pushed #{cmd[1]}"
  when "pop"
    val = stack.pop
    puts val.nil? ? "empty" : "popped #{val}"
  when "peek"
    val = stack.peek
    puts val.nil? ? "empty" : "top #{val}"
  when "size"
    puts stack.size
  when "empty"
    puts stack.empty?
  end
end

questions.title: Bank Account Multi Operation Statement
questions.description:
An `Account` class stores `@balance` and a `@transactions` array (both set in `initialize`). Instance methods `deposit(amount)` and `withdraw(amount)` mutate both. The `statement` method prints `Balance: <bal>`, `Transactions: <count>`, and the comma-joined transaction labels (only if any). Read initial balance, then n, then n `deposit X` or `withdraw X` commands.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer balance. Line 2: integer n. Next n lines: `deposit X` or `withdraw X`.

Output Format:
Two or three lines from `statement`.

Constraints:
0 <= balance, amounts <= 1000000; 0 <= n <= 100.
questions.whitelist: def initialize, def deposit, def withdraw, def statement
questions.sourcecode:
class Account
  def initialize(balance)
    @balance = balance
    @transactions = []
  end
  def deposit(amount)
    @balance += amount
    @transactions << "+#{amount}"
  end
  def withdraw(amount)
    @balance -= amount
    @transactions << "-#{amount}"
  end
  def statement
    puts "Balance: #{@balance}"
    puts "Transactions: #{@transactions.length}"
    puts @transactions.join(",") if @transactions.any?
  end
end
bal = gets.to_i
acct = Account.new(bal)
n = gets.to_i
n.times do
  op, amt = gets.split
  if op == "deposit"
    acct.deposit(amt.to_i)
  elsif op == "withdraw"
    acct.withdraw(amt.to_i)
  end
end
acct.statement

questions.title: Inventory self Empty Factory
questions.description:
An `Inventory` class stores `@items` (hash) set in `initialize`. The class method `self.empty` returns a new instance. The instance method `add(name, qty)` accumulates quantities; `total` returns the sum. Read n then n `name qty` pairs. Use `Inventory.empty` to construct, then print the total quantity.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: `name qty` separated by space.

Output Format:
The integer total quantity.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; 0 <= qty <= 10000; name length 1..20.
questions.whitelist: def self.empty, def add, def total
questions.sourcecode:
class Inventory
  def initialize
    @items = {}
  end
  def self.empty
    new
  end
  def add(name, qty)
    @items[name] = (@items[name] || 0) + qty
  end
  def total
    t = 0
    @items.each { |name, qty| t += qty }
    t
  end
end
n = gets.to_i
inv = Inventory.empty
n.times do
  name, qty = gets.split
  inv.add(name, qty.to_i)
end
puts inv.total
